VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed bound $\overline P_1(V)\ge 2\overline q(V)-2$ is very likely not the sharp bound for surfaces that are not of maximal Albanese dimension, though I could not verify the exact published polynomial.

- **Analogy with the projective case.** For smooth projective surfaces, the Debarre-type bound $p_g\ge 2q-4$ is for maximal Albanese dimension. Surfaces that fiber over a curve of genus $b$ (with $q=b$ and fibers of genus $\ge 2$) satisfy $p_g\ge (g-1)(b-1)$, which is only about $q-1$. So the non-maximal case should admit a weaker linear bound, not a stronger one.
- **Test examples I checked.** Products $C\times\mathbb P^1$ minus three fibers and $C\times C^*$ both have maximal log-Albanese dimension, so they do not test the non-maximal case. Products of this kind with $\mathbb P^1$ or $C^*$ factors give $\overline P_1 = 2\overline q-4$ or $2\overline q-2$ in the cases I computed, but they are excluded here. I did not find a non-maximal example that attains $2q-2$.
- **Likely form.** My recollection, which I could not confirm, is a bound of the form $\overline P_1(V)\ge \overline q(V)-2$ in the non-maximal case, with $2\overline q-4$ for maximal Albanese dimension.

CONFIDENCE: 3
